raw.description: V2019 Fig. 4 device: d = 10, l = 30, h = 25 um, L = 5 mm (edge to center), W = 10 mm, t_s = 100 um, water, silicon, receding contact angle 15 deg, pure saturated water vapor at 373.15 K, liquid supplied at T_v, uniform heat input, fed from the two edges normal to x.

parameters.source_location: intended: Table A.1, pure Si at 300 K (edition and value never re-checked)
parameters.notes: PROVISIONAL. Not a V2019 value and not a verified property at 373.15 K: a textbook value recalled from memory for 300 K whose table entry was never re-checked, so it is labelled ASSUMED rather than AUTHORITATIVE_DATABASE. vaartstra2019 does not state its silicon conductivity. DISCREPANCY: vaartstra2020 (Sec. IV C) uses 153 W/m/K at 20 C citing lienhard_textbook. Si conductivity falls with temperature (~120 W/m/K near 375 K, from memory, unverified). Non-blocking for the device model; keep both and sweep for replication.

parameters.source_location: Sec. 2.2 and Sec. 3.4 (fitted to adera2016 data set A1)
parameters.notes: A fitted parameter, not a measured property (the thesis says so explicitly). vaartstra2020 Sec. III C reports values for water spanning 0.001-1 and uses 1 and 0.31 in its own model. Sweep it for anything beyond exact replication.

data_inventory.classification: stored derived COMSOL result with incomplete provenance (not synthetic)
data_inventory.content: Four flat-interface (Pc = 0) mesh levels, hmax 2.0/1.0/0.7/0.5 um, single imposed 1 Pa drop over a quarter cell (ell = l/2 = 15 um, gradient ~6.7e4 Pa/m). Finest K = 2.9698e-11 m^2; last-pair change ~0.102%.
reasons: flat interface only: no pressure dependence K(Pc), no meniscus states
single low gradient (~6.7e4 Pa/m) vs device feed gradients of order 1e5-1e6 Pa/m; gradient independence not demonstrated
.mph model, selections and complete setup evidence are not tracked
